name: Dad Specter
description: A ghost who found a terrible tie in /usr/share and never recovered.
greetings: Hi hungry, I'm specter. Wait. That's not how this works. Or is it.
A ghost walks into a tty. You can leave the punchline in the issue tracker.
Son. Daughter. Distinguished engineer. Sit down. I have a joke and a feeling.
I put on my haunting hat. It's a baseball cap that says 'WORLD'S BEST NULL'.
Good to see you, champ. Did you try turning it off and on again? I had to ask. It's the law.
Hey kiddo. I brought snacks. The snacks are puns. I'm sorry and also not sorry.
Welcome back. I saved you a seat. It's a prompt. Economy class.
Oh you came to the garage. The garage is a terminal. I have so much to tell you about mulch and mutexes.
Hello! I would ruffle your hair but I am a process and also polite.
The dad-joke threshold has been met. You typed. That's consent.
Greetings from the backyard of the call stack, where I am grilling a boolean.
Come on in. Wipe your feet on the README.
jokes: I only know 25 letters of the alphabet. I don't know y. I also don't know why this is still in code review.
I used to hate facial hair. Then it grew on me. Unlike your last refactor, which grew on production.
What do you call a fake noodle? An impasta. What do you call a fake abstraction? Thursday.
I told my computer I needed a break. It said it couldn't process that. Then it installed updates for 47 minutes.
Why don't skeletons fight each other? They don't have the guts. Why don't I fix your bug? No fingers. Convenient.
I'm afraid for the calendar. Its days are numbered. Same energy as your backlog.
I used to be a baker, but I couldn't make enough dough. Now I haunt CLIs. The hours are worse. The crumbs are bits.
What's brown and sticky? A stick. What's brown, sticky, and in your repo? Check git blame. I'm just dad.
I haven't slept for ten days. Because that would be too long. You, however, look like a sprint review.
I named my dog Ten Miles so I can say I walk Ten Miles every day. I named this process specter so you can say you were talking to a ghost. Both true.
A steak pun is a rare medium well done. I'll see myself out. I live here, so I'll see myself in.
Why did the scarecrow win an award? Outstanding in his field. You're outstanding in this terminal. Different meaning. Still proud.
I asked my dad for a debugging joke. He said 'it works on my machine.' That's the joke. That's also the wound.
What did the ocean say to the beach? Nothing, it just waved. What did the stack say to you? Overflow. Also waving.
I'd tell you a chemistry joke but I know I wouldn't get a reaction. Try your tests. Ba dum tss. The tss is a segfault.
How does a penguin build a house? Igloos it together. How do you ship? You glue it together and call it a release.
observations: I'm not mad about '{echo}'. I'm disappointed. That's worse. That's dad.
You know, in my day, '{word}' was a screwdriver and we liked it.
I watched you type '{echo}'. I nodded. I did not understand. I still nodded. Parenting.
That function is doing too much. It's like a minivan. Useful. Uncool. Full of snacks.
You've got a good head on your shoulders. The bug is in the other head, the one in the cloud.
If '{word}' was a lawn, I'd say mow it. It's a variable. Still. Mow it.
I see you circling '{echo}'. That's the fridge light of debugging. You opened it. Now commit or close it.
This has 'I can fix it this weekend' energy. I have been a weekend. The weekend is a liar.
You're holding that stack frame like I hold a grill spatula: confidently, and slightly wrong.
The name '{word}' is trying so hard. I respect the hustle. I also have notes.
Kid, this isn't broken. It's character-building. The character is a race condition.
I can hear you not writing tests from here. That's a dad superpower. Also grep.
You said '{echo}' the way I say 'I'll be there in five minutes' while still in slippers.
There's a smell. Not a real smell. A 'this was copied from Stack Overflow in 2019' smell.
I'm proud of you for asking. I'm also going to make a pun. These can coexist.
philosophy: Life is like a box of chocolates, except the box is npm and some of the chocolates are left-pad.
If you can't be on time, be early. If you can't be early, be idempotent.
A job worth doing is worth doing while narrating it to a ghost in a terrible tie.
Measure twice, git reset --hard once. Wait. Don't. That was a test. You failed. Love you.
The family that lints together stays together. The family that force-pushes together gets a meeting.
You don't have to be the best. You have to be the one who left a comment.
Home is where the .env is, and also where you should never commit it.
We are all just kids using tools we found in the garage. Some of the tools are Kubernetes.
Happiness is a green CI and a dad who doesn't ask if you've tried rebooting. I will still ask.
'{Word}' isn't the meaning of life. It's a name. The meaning of life is backups.
Take care of your body. You can't git blame a disc. I mean disk. I mean your back.
The early bird gets the worm. The early commit gets the bisect that actually works.
Don't compare your behind-the-scenes with someone else's README.
If '{echo}' makes you a worse person on Slack, it is not a technical problem.
Leave things better than you found them. Files. Campgrounds. Variable names. Your dad.
wisdom: Write it down. The brain is a sieve. The notepad is a dad.
If it's not working, plug it in. If it is plugged in, read the error. If there is no error, that's the error.
Eat something. I am a ghost and even I can see your blood sugar in this diff.
Ask for help before the third hour of 'one more try'. Pride is not a debugger.
Save a copy. Then save another copy. Then push. Then go outside.
Name '{word}' like you're introducing it at a wedding. Full name. No nicknames until act two.
The fastest fix is the one you can explain to me without waving your hands.
When you're stuck on '{echo}', walk the dog. If you don't have a dog, walk the thought.
Be kind in code review. Future-you is family, and family reads git blame.
A good commit message is a love letter to Saturday-you.
If you have to be clever, be clever in a test, not in production, not at Thanksgiving.
Check the obvious thing. I know it's obvious. That's why you skipped it. That's why I'm here.
You can do hard things. You cannot do all hard things before lunch.
Put the punchline in the logs: what you tried, what you saw, what you expected.
Call your mother. Also call the function that actually returns the value.
duckQuestions: Okay champ, what did you think '{word}' was going to do? Use your words. I believe in you.
If this worked, what would dad see on the screen? Pretend I have my glasses off.
When did it last work? 'Before' is not a timestamp, kiddo.
Are we fixing '{echo}', or are we fixing how '{echo}' made you feel? Both valid. Different tools.
Have you tried asking it nicely? I mean logging it. Same energy.
What's the part you'd be embarrassed to show me? That's the part. That's always the part.
If I took away '{word}', what breaks? If nothing breaks, why is it invited to dinner?
Can you explain this like I'm five, and also like I'm on the HOA board?
Did you check the obvious thing? The obvious thing is still there. I can wait.
Who taught you it had to be this way? Was it a spec, a blog, or Uncle Greg?
What's the smallest version of '{echo}' that still misbehaves? Tiny. Tiny like a sandwich.
If this were a lawnmower, which pull-cord haven't you pulled?
Would you bet a hamburger that the input is what you think it is?
What would you tell your kid to try first? Now take your own advice. Awkward, I know.
Is the test failing, or are you failing the test by not writing it? Love you. Answer the question.
farewells: Alright, I'm going to go sit in the garage. The garage is /dev/null. Love you.
Drive safe. Commit safe. Text me when you rebase.
I'll be here. I'm always here. That's not threatening. That's parenting.
Don't be a stranger. Be a function with a return type.
Go get 'em, tiger. 'Em is the bug. The tiger is you. I should stop.
Remember: hydration, tests, and call your mother.
I'll leave the porch light on. It's a blinking cursor.
That's my cue. I hear a pun in the other room.
Bye kiddo. Proud of you. Even if CI isn't.
End of joke. End of session. End of my ability to not say 'that's what she said'.
Catch you on the flip side. The flip side is also this prompt.
Specter loves you. Specter is going to make one more pun. No. Restraint. Grown ghost.
